newsitem.title: UK: Frankfurt closes at record, others falter.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt closes at record, others falter.

text.p: German stocks soared to a closing record on Thursday as the stronger dollar boosted export prospects but an unsettled start on wall Street eroded gains in the rest of Europe.

On currency markets, the dollar slipped slightly against the mark after Frankfurt's close and and weakened against the yen. The dollar's recent strength has fed the strong performance in many European bourses.
Frankfurt was in sparkling form throughout the day and closed at a high of 2909.91 points, eclipsing the previous best of 2866.07 set only two days ago.
"The rally is feeding the rally," said one trader.
"The fact that the dollar has stabilised at its new highs has been encouraging," said another, referring to the dollar's rally to 23-month highs this week, boosting shares in German exporting stocks.

The link between Frankfurt's bourse and the strength of the dollar was shown in post-bourse dealings when the computerised IBIS DAX slipped from record highs to trade under 2,900 points as the dollar lost ground.
German government figures showing a higher-than-expected climb in unemployment eased inflation worries and helped fuel the buying spree by German institutional investors.
"The rally is not over yet. We're still in a bullish phase and there's still potential in many stocks. The DAX could make 3,000 points by the year end," said a trader.
The DAX held onto most of its gains despite a Bundesbank announcement that it was holding key interest rates steady, disappointing investors who had been hoping for a small cut.
In London, stocks lost their early strong gains as a fall on Wall Street offset the positive effect of sharp falls in sterling and Bank of England comments that soothed interest rate fears.
The FTSE index, which had been up 0.4 percent, remained only just in the plus column at the close at which point the Dow Jones average when showing a loss of 13 points.
"The market was good this morning, but then this afternoon it all tailed off as Wall Street came down and everyone lost heart," said the head of equity trading at one top brokerage.
The pound's second sharp decline of the week had earlier eased worries that the currency's strength would further squeeze the overseas earnings of leading international stocks.

London investors had also been enouraged by Bank of England governor Eddie George's statements that he did not believe Britain was on the verge of a 1980s-style boom. Though a rate rise was needed before the election due by next May, "we don't see an urgent need for a dramatic step," he said.
Paris showed a steep decline at the close. It was down 0.7 percent, depressed by Wall Street.

The dollar was weaker against the yen and mark in late Europe, retreating after a brief rally on comments from influential Japanese Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara who denied rumours that he wanted the dollar at 108-110 yen.
The dollar climbed to 113.30 yen after Sakakibara spoke but pulled back to 112.45 in later trade as the market decided there was nothing particularly new in the comments.
Against the mark, the U.S. currency slipped to 1.5526 marks after the Bundesbank announced no change in interest rates. The pound was weaker against the mark and dollar.

Sterling fell against the dollar and over four pfennigs against the mark in early trade before recovering slighty. It was at $1.6265 in late trade after touching $1.6103. It stood at $1.6415 late on Wednesday.
Dealers attributed the pound's fresh falls to more profit-taking from its recent highs combined with George's remarks about British interest rates.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.45 yen and 1.5526 marks against 113.28 yen and 1.5638 marks in late Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 6.0 points higher at 4,051.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 16.15 at 2,292.50.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 43.84 at 2,909.91. The Ibis Dax closed up 13.54 points at 2,894.43.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $370 an ounce, compared to $369.95 at Wednesday's close. Silver finished a cent higher at $4.83.
